title: Shabana Azmi Has Never Played a Villain in 50 Years. Awarapan 2 Just Changed That.
excerpt: The five-time National Award winner joins Emraan Hashmi's underworld sequel as Nafisa — a criminal matriarch so dangerous she rewrites the entire story. At 75, she calls it 'a moral about-turn.' We call it overdue.
body:
In five decades and over 150 films, **Shabana Azmi** has been a freedom fighter, a sex worker, a grieving mother, a political prisoner, and a woman scorned in ways that would make Greek tragedy blush. She has never — not once — played the villain.

Until now.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=4Px6H3KDxkM</youtube>


**Vishesh Films** announced this week that Azmi has been cast as **Nafisa**, the central antagonist in **Awarapan 2**, the long-awaited sequel to the 2007 cult romantic thriller. The film stars **Emraan Hashmi** returning as Shivam Malik, the gangster who barely survived the first film's devastating climax, alongside **Disha Patani**. Directed by **Nitin Kakkar** and written by **Bilal Siddiqui**, the sequel releases in cinemas on **August 14, 2026** — Independence Day weekend, naturally.

The announcement arrived with a photograph of Azmi and a statement from producer **Vishesh Bhatt** that read:

> "Nafisa could only ever be Shabana ji. She came home on her birthday, and everything found its place. We are deeply honored to welcome the National Award-winning legend to the franchise, marking the first antagonist role of her monumental career."

Azmi joined the cast on September 18, 2025 — her birthday — which feels almost too poetic for a Bhatt production, but here we are.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZcf25njC-y/

The character of Nafisa was created by writer Siddiqui as a quietly authoritative figure within the criminal underworld — someone whose entrance into the story fundamentally alters the trajectory of Shivam's life. It was Vishesh Bhatt who made the pivotal decision to reimagine the role as a woman, a move that reframed both the character and the entire film around her presence. Once that decision was made, the casting was never in question.

When first asked about the role, Azmi responded with characteristic wit:

> "Where did you hear this? I'm not supposed to speak about it. Yes, it is quite a moral about-turn. I have always wanted to play the villain. Mogambo khush hua."

That *Mr. India* reference alone is worth the price of admission.

Azmi's connection to the Bhatt family runs decades deep. She starred in **Mahesh Bhatt's** *Arth* in 1982, one of the defining works of parallel Hindi cinema — a film about love, betrayal, and creative ego that remains devastatingly relevant 44 years later. Working with his nephew Vishesh on *Awarapan 2* adds another chapter to a professional bond that has outlasted most Bollywood dynasties. And in a detail that collapses the industry's entire generational timeline, Azmi recalls working with Emraan Hashmi's grandmother, actress **Purnima**, in *Fakira* back in 1976. "It's my first time collaborating with Emraan, whom I've seen as a child," she shared. Fifty years between those two sentences. Only Bollywood.

For those who remember the original *Awarapan*, its enduring appeal rests on something commercial Hindi cinema rarely gets right: genuine emotional devastation. Hashmi's Shivam was a character who loved someone he could never have and paid for it with nearly everything. The melancholic "Toh Phir Aao" became one of the decade's most-played heartbreak anthems. The sequel's creative challenge is to take that broken man and pit him against an adversary compelling enough to justify reopening his story. In Shabana Azmi, they haven't just found an adversary — they've found a force of nature.

The film has completed shooting across Mumbai, Singapore, and international locations. Hashmi has described the sequel as having "crazy music and intense scenes," which, coming from the man who built his career on Bollywood's most brooding romantic sequences, is a statement worth taking seriously.

For diaspora audiences, *Awarapan* holds genuine cult status — it's one of those mid-2000s films that found its truest audience not in Indian theaters but on late-night TV replays, YouTube uploads, and nostalgic conversations at desi dinner parties. The prospect of a sequel headlined by a five-time National Award winner playing the villain, dropping on Independence Day weekend in theaters worldwide, is the kind of event that turns a routine mid-August release into appointment viewing.

At 75, Shabana Azmi is doing what most actors half her age refuse to do: something genuinely new. In an industry that runs on comfort zones and brand safety, watching a veteran with nothing left to prove crack her knuckles and invoke Mogambo is exactly the energy 2026 needs.

*Awarapan 2* releases in cinemas on August 14, 2026. Starring Emraan Hashmi, Shabana Azmi, and Disha Patani. Directed by Nitin Kakkar. Written by Bilal Siddiqui. Produced by Vishesh Bhatt.
